title: Randomized competitive ratio of list update
formal: Determine \(\rho_{\rm LU}=\inf\{r\ge1:\text{ randomized online list update is }r\text{-competitive}\}\) against an oblivious adversary in the full-cost model below. The benchmark accepts a real approximation with absolute error at most \(1/100\).
definitions: For each \(n\ge1\), the input is a fixed set of \(n\) distinct items, an initial linear order \(L_0\), and any finite request sequence \(\sigma\) fixed independently of the algorithm’s randomness. Access to the item currently at position \(i\), counting from one, costs \(i\). After accessing an item, it may be moved toward the front by any distance for free. Any other swap of two adjacent items costs one. The algorithm serves each request before seeing the next. Offline OPT knows the sequence, starts in the same \(L_0\), and pays under exactly the same rules. A ratio \(r\) is achievable if, for every \(n,L_0\), an online randomized rule and a finite \(\beta\ge0\) exist such that \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{cost}_A(\sigma)]\le r\operatorname{OPT}(\sigma)+\beta\) for every \(\sigma\). The rule and \(\beta\) may depend on \(n,L_0,r\), but not on future requests; there is no computational-time constraint on choosing legal rearrangements. The infimum need not be attained. The constant is dimensionless.
why: Even for an elementary self-organizing list, the optimal benefit of randomization in competitive performance is unknown.

context_blocks.text: The 2025 paper records a lower bound of 1.5 and an upper bound of 1.6 for randomized list update. Deterministic move-to-front has competitive ratio 2.
The benchmark concerns the ordinary model with no predictions or advice. The cited paper studies prediction extensions while documenting the classical baseline.

answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real number \(a\) and a complete Lean-checked proof that \(|a-\rho_{\rm LU}|\le1/100\). Matching upper and lower bounds implying this error qualify; the ratio need not be attained by one algorithm. An uncertified experiment or a bound outside this precision is insufficient.
